title: A supplied finite local presentation gives a finitely presented stalk
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $F$ a module sheaf, $x\in U\subseteq X$ an open neighborhood. Suppose a finite presentation $P$ of $F|_U$ is supplied, with finite generator and relation index sets [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], using slice-site restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then the module stalk $F_x$ over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is finitely presented: it is the quotient of a finite free module by a finitely generated submodule.

source.place: Tag 01CP, proof, third paragraph: the right exact source-stalk presentation; Definition 01BN.

proof.text: The forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves colimits. Abelian sheaf stalks are left adjoints to skyscrapers. Forgetting modules reflects colimits, so the module stalk functor preserves the coproducts and cokernel defining the presentation.

Identify the unit stalk with the regular module through the forgetful-colimit isomorphism. Prove scalar compatibility on simultaneous scalar and vector germs. Finite coproduct preservation identifies free stalks with finite products of regular modules. Applying the stalk functor to P.isColimit gives a surjection with kernel the image of the finite relation module. Apply Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective and Submodule.fg_range.

Pass from the slice site to the open subspace through the module equivalence. Transport scalars along the inverse ring-stalk isomorphism; restriction of scalars along a ring equivalence preserves colimits and takes the regular module to the regular module. Apply the preceding argument, then transfer finite presentation along the linear restriction-stalk isomorphism.

theorem finitePresentation_stalk_of_localPresentation
    (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (F : Modules X) (x : X)
    (U : Opens X) (_hxU : x ∈ U)
    (P : (F.over U).Presentation) [P.IsFinite] :
    Module.FinitePresentation (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj F)
